classification.difficultyReason: Find an auxiliary angle from a right angle, then combine opposite-angle equality with the quadrilateral angle sum.

content.prompt: Determine the value of $a$ in this diagram. Explain your reasoning.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 13 diagram, below the stem on the left
spec.description: Unshaded slanted parallelogram with matching single and double parallel arrows, a dashed lower-left-to-upper-right diagonal, vertical and horizontal reference rays, a right-angle square, external angles 32° and 7°, and upper-left interior angle a°.
spec.mathematics: The lower side is 7° above horizontal and the left side is 32° from vertical. Their included interior angle is 51°. Opposite sides are parallel. Coordinates reconstruct these angle relationships without supplying lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the auxiliary angle b and calculated values appear only in the worked answer.

answer.short: $a=129^{\circ}$. The lower-left angle is $90^{\circ}-32^{\circ}-7^{\circ}=51^{\circ}$; opposite angles are equal and the four interior angles sum to $360^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
Let $b$ be the lower-left interior angle. The reference rays form a right angle.
$$\begin{align*}b&=90^{\circ}-32^{\circ}-7^{\circ}\\b&=51^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The parallel marks show a parallelogram, so opposite angles are equal. Using the quadrilateral angle sum:
$$\begin{align*}2a+2b&=360^{\circ}\\2a&=360^{\circ}-2(51^{\circ})\\2a&=258^{\circ}\\a&=129^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
